record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: When galaxies or compact galaxy groups appear connected by filaments, radio material, emission structures, or positional alignments but have strongly discordant redshifts, are those systems chance projections along the line of sight, or do they indicate physical associations in which at least some galaxy redshifts are non-cosmological?

evidence.quote: There are some cases in which “apparently” connected or interacting galaxies have different redshifts[81, 26, 82]. One of the most famous cases is Stephan’s quintet(SQ)[83].

There is also a Hα-filament which is extending throughout NGC 7320 with velocity at 6500 km/s instead of 800 km/s expected for this galaxy[86], which is somewhat unlikely to be there by chance. The conclusions about SQ are not clear yet.

Example: the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 7603 (z = 0.029) appears connected to a companion galaxy (z = 0.056) and along the thin filament there are two further HII-galaxies with redshifts 0.24 and 0.39[92, 93], which makes the system much more unprobable in terms of cosmological redshifts.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider observed configurations in which two or more galaxies (or compact galaxy groups) appear physically connected — by luminous filaments, neutral or ionized gas bridges, radio continuum structures, tidal-like emission features, or by striking positional alignments — yet possess strongly discordant spectroscopic redshifts (e.g., a low-redshift Seyfert galaxy apparently connected by a narrow filament to companion objects with much larger redshifts, as in systems of Stephan's-quintet type or in the NGC 7603 system, where the principal galaxy has z ≈ 0.029 while objects along an apparent connecting filament have z ≈ 0.056, 0.24, and 0.39).

Question: For such systems of apparently connected but redshift-discordant galaxies, determine whether the observed configurations are explained by chance superpositions of physically unrelated objects along the line of sight (so that all redshifts may be interpreted as ordinary cosmological recession velocities consistent with Hubble's law), or whether they constitute genuine physical associations in which at least some of the constituent redshifts must be non-cosmological in origin (i.e., not produced by cosmic expansion alone, but by some other mechanism such as ejection, intrinsic redshifts, or unknown physics).

A complete answer should either (a) provide a statistically defensible mechanism (e.g., projection probabilities, gravitational lensing, selection effects) that accounts for all known cases under the standard cosmological interpretation of redshift, or (b) establish, via observational or theoretical evidence, that at least one such system requires a non-cosmological component of redshift.
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up observational studies (e.g., the NGC 7603 field study by López-Corredoira & Gutiérrez, A&A 2004) confirmed the discordant redshifts of objects along the connecting filament and estimated the chance-projection probability for the NGC 7603 configuration at roughly 3×10⁻⁹, while finding gravitational macro- and micro-lensing to be unsatisfactory explanations. The non-cosmological-redshift hypothesis could not be ruled out but lacks an accepted physical mechanism. The question therefore remains unresolved within the standard cosmological framework.

status_evidence.title: The field surrounding NGC 7603: Cosmological or non-cosmological redshifts?
status_evidence.snippet: Four galaxies apparently connected by a filament with discordant redshifts; probability of chance projection ~3×10⁻⁹; lensing explanations disfavored; non-cosmological redshift cannot be rejected.
status_evidence.claim: Statistical chance projection is extremely unlikely and standard explanations fail, leaving the issue unresolved.

status_evidence.title: What's the present status of anomalous redshifts such as NGC 7603?
status_evidence.snippet: Community discussion indicating the status of NGC 7603-like anomalous redshift systems remains debated.
status_evidence.claim: The status of anomalous-redshift cases is still under discussion in the astronomical community.

status_evidence.title: [astro-ph/0401147] The field surrounding NGC 7603
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms redshifts of emission-line objects on the filament; alternative explanations (clusters along LOS, macro/micro lensing) deemed unlikely.
status_evidence.claim: Standard mechanisms for explaining the system have been examined and found inadequate, but no definitive resolution is given.
